title: Ketanomocke
summary: Ketanomocke, also written Ketewamoke and Ketan-om-muck, is associated with Huntington and interpreted as a shoreline or beach placename.
address_label: General Huntington / East Northport area, Suffolk County, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general point near the Huntington and East Northport area based on Tooker, Langhans, and Huntington records; offset slightly for map visibility and not an exact village coordinate.
introduction_content: Ketanomocke is a Huntington-area placename recorded in several forms, including Ketewamoke and Ketan-om-muck. The surviving explanation points readers to Arhakaamunk because of earlier confusion between the names.
translation_content:
Ketan-om-muck is explained as referring to a place where the sea flows, the shore, or a beach. Recorded forms include Ketanomocke and Ketewamoke. The interpretation should not be treated as a settled one-word translation.

Why Place Names Matter

“The value of place names is that they reflect specific localities, landmarks, and identities in otherwise amorphous spaces and environments.”

— V. R. Savage, Place Names (2009), International Encyclopedia of Human Geography overview
land_loss_content: Ketanomocke preserves a shoreline placename and a Huntington-area community reference that colonial records connected to Native leadership and land transactions. Reading it alongside related place names helps show how Indigenous geography remained visible in records even as English town names and property boundaries took hold.
whereintheworld_content: Ketanomocke is associated broadly with the modern Huntington and East Northport area. The sources do not establish an exact historic village location.
